newsitem.title: UK: Guzzling gods, prudish ghosts in 1996 weird record.
newsitem.headline: Guzzling gods, prudish ghosts in 1996 weird record.

text.p: The past year has been a strange one for many people, with Hindu icons guzzling India's milk supplies, sheep found dangling from trees in New Zealand and a stampede of snails halting trains in Morocco.

Britain's Fortean Times, an annual chronicle of weird happenings published this week, records dozens of sightings of unidentified flying objects, reports of strange creatures preying on humans as well as farm animals and an array of astonishing coincidences.
For those fearful of invasion from outer space, the back page of the 1996 edition advertises a testing kit for women who fear they have been impregnated by aliens.
The edition said Puerto Rican authorities are hunting a "fanged, kangaroo-like entity with bulging red eyes and spines" which is blamed for the bloody deaths of hundreds of farm animals.
Meanwhile, the men of Zanzibar are living in fear of a huge, bat-like creature with one eye, which swoops into their houses at night and rapes them.
The book tells of a prudish ghost who drove a married couple to making love in a tent in their garden because it let out howls of protest whenever they got passionate in the bedroom.
There is also a man so desperate for company he abducted two women at gunpoint, and forced them to buy Twinkie snacks then accompany him on a tour of Christmas lights.
The book says that silicone breast implants offer a useful benefit, after hearing of a Florida stripper whose fake breasts saved her life by deflecting a bullet fired from the audience.
Milk supplies ran out in much of northern India after the god Ganesh was said to have taken to drinking it and the Hindu faithful gathered to feed spoonful after spoonful to the icons.
New Zealanders were baffled when dozens of sheep were found dangling in a forest 100 feet (30 metres) from the ground. A pilot later admitted they had fallen from his helicopter.

They were not the only animals to hit the Fortean headlines. A British farmer used an earth-moving vehicle to take two pigs to slaughter, but when he got out of the driving seat with one of the beasts, the other shuffled over and set the vehicle in motion, pinning the farmer to the road.
A dog in the Czech republic saved human lives by peeing on a plastic explosive bomb left in a shop doorway.
A sadder tale is that of the dog in Nepal which committed suicide by throwing itself into a pond three days after his 12-year-old master drowned.
